sections.label: CJRA criminal justice changes
sections.summary: The CJRA introduced video recording of interviews, a procedure to reopen exhausted criminal cases, and changes to evidence disclosure and sentencing powers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: CJRA introduced, amongst other things, the video recording of interviews in investigations and a statutory procedure for the reopening of criminal cases where all appeals had been exhausted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Changes were also made to disclosure of evidence in criminal proceedings and to the sentencing powers of the Court, including to the sentence of Reformative Training.

sections.label: VRI offences and evidence redaction
sections.summary: The Bill lets prescribed agencies investigate VRI-related offences and lets the Police or Prosecution redact sensitive information before disclosure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As such, the Bill will allow prescribed law enforcement agencies which already have the power to take VRI statements to investigate any VRI-related offences relating to the statements they take.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The second amendment will allow the Police or the Prosecution to redact sensitive information from any document or thing relating to a criminal case before disclosing it to the Defence or other persons.

sections.label: Reformative Training backdating and minimum period
sections.summary: An amendment proposes that RT sentences cannot be backdated, and the Court may set the minimum period at 12 or six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: An amendment is proposed to provide that an RT sentence cannot be backdated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: What this means is that even if an offender was remanded before sentence, any RT sentence imposed cannot be backdated to take the remand period into account.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The period used to be 18 months, but under those amendments, the Court is given the discretion to set the minimum period at either 12 months or six months depending on the nature of the rehabilitation required.

sections.label: Agencies minimising remand for RT
sections.summary: The Police and Attorney-General's Chambers will work together to avoid or minimise remand where RT is a possible sentence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To address this, the relevant agencies, such as the Police and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC), will work together to ensure that where RT is a possible sentence, remand is either avoided or minimised where possible.

sections.label: Support with clarification requests
sections.summary: The speaker moves the motion, supports the amendments, and asks the Ministry to clarify matters on VRIs and RT sentences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am generally supportive of the amendments proposed, but I would like the Ministry to clarify two matters, firstly, relating to VRIs and, secondly, on RT sentences.

sections.label: VRI agency use and backdating removal
sections.summary: The Minister is asked which agencies use VRI and for what offences, and Clause 6 removes the judge's right to backdate custody.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To get a sense of how widespread the use of VRI is among our law enforcement agencies, could the Minister inform the House as to which agencies have commenced using VRI, and for what kinds of offences?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill basically removes the right of the sentencing judge to backdate the period of custody to an earlier date.

sections.label: Avoiding or minimising remand
sections.summary: The passage asks what practical steps will be taken to avoid or minimise remand, as MinLaw has stated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to avoid or minimise remand as MinLaw has stated, what practical things will be done?

sections.label: Investigating VRI-related offences
sections.summary: Clause 3 of the Bill allows officers of prescribed law enforcement agencies to investigate offences relating to VRIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In terms of investigations, clause 3 of the Bill allows officers of prescribed law enforcement agencies to investigate offences relating to VRIs.

sections.label: Non-disclosure of sensitive information
sections.summary: Clause 9 provides for non-disclosure of sensitive information and a process for it, balancing the accused's rights with others' interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Moving on to amendments relating to the pre-trial and trial stages, clause 9 provides for the non-disclosure of sensitive information and a process for it, that is, seeking a balance between the accused’s rights and interests with those of others.

sections.label: Removing backdating of RT
sections.summary: Clause 6 removes the Courts' ability to backdate RT, which the High Court said could undermine the programme's effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 6 removes the ability of the Courts to backdate RT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As the Singapore High Court in the case of Nur Azilah bte Ithnin vv Public Prosecutor opined, backdating RT will shorten the period of training and could undermine or hinder the effectiveness of such a programme.

sections.label: Training and inter-agency workgroup
sections.summary: Agencies will assess needed training before bringing changes into force, overseen by an inter-agency workgroup for uniform VRI implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As with all legislative amendments, before bringing the changes into force, the relevant agencies will assess what kind of training or preparation is needed and will get that done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is an inter-agency workgroup comprising the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), MinLaw, AGC, the Police and other law enforcement agencies which oversees the development of policies, operational procedures and also training plans to ensure uniformity in VRI implementation across the agencies.

sections.label: VRI use and feedback
sections.summary: VRI has been used in rape and drug trafficking investigations, with useful feedback, but no VRI recording has yet been used as evidence in Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: VRI has been used by the Serious Sexual Crime Branch of the Criminal Investigation Department in investigations into rape, and by the Central Narcotics Bureau to investigate certain drug trafficking offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Early feedback from the ground and from these agencies is that VRI is useful to investigators and our officers are confident in the VRI system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So far, there has not yet been a case where a VRI recording has been used as evidence in Court.

sections.label: Defence application without procedural barrier
sections.summary: The Defence may apply for the Court's determination without any procedural barrier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Defence may apply for the Court’s determination without any procedural barrier.

sections.label: Prosecution disclosure obligations and rebuttable presumption
sections.summary: Courts set procedures balancing competing interests; the apex Court held the presumption of Prosecution compliance with disclosure obligations can be rebutted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Courts have set down detailed procedures to fairly balance the competing interests in this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And the High Court's decision in Winston Lee's case was then subsequently brought before the Court of Appeal in a Criminal Reference, and our apex Court stated that while the Public Prosecutor is presumed to have complied with his disclosure obligations on account of his constitutional office, this presumption can be rebutted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Once the Defence satisfies the Court that there are reasonable grounds for belief that the Prosecution has failed to comply with its Kadar obligation, the Court will look to the Prosecution to show that it has complied.

sections.label: RT sentence start date confirmation
sections.summary: Ms Sylvia Lim asked for confirmation that a Court will not have an RT sentence take effect later than the date passed if the offender is in pre-sentence remand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked for confirmation that a Court will not have an RT sentence take effect on a date later than the date it was passed if the offender is already in pre-sentence remand, as I understand the question.

sections.label: CT for adult repeat offenders
sections.summary: CT applies to adult repeat offenders with serious previous convictions, with sentences of five to 14 years and no remission entitlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: CT applies to adult offenders – as opposed to RT – who have committed one or more offences with maximum sentences of two years' imprisonment or more, and who also have relatively serious previous convictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These adult repeat offenders can be sentenced to CT for a minimum of five and a maximum of 14 years, without entitlement to remission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Considering the long minimum duration of CT sentences, there is less risk that backdating of such sentences will interfere with any rehabilitative efforts during the sentence.
